newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Bonn clears way for Postbank privatisaion.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bonn clears way for Postbank privatisaion.

text.p: The German government on Friday said it will allow the Post Office to take a stake of up to 17.5 percent in Deutsche Postbank AG, clearing the way for the privatisation of banking arm of the postal authority later this year.
The deal reached by the governing coalition parties denies the Post Office effective control of the bank and appears to be a victory for the liberal Free Democrats (FDP).
The junior partners in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition had opposed the Post Office's bid for control of Postbank in months of wrangling with Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU).
Both the Post Office and Postbank, which have argued heatedly over how much they owe each other, said they were satisfied with the compromise.
But the coalition must now decide whose allies will split up the rest of the postal banking arm -- those favoured by the Post Office, or those chosen by Postbank itself.
A sale of 75 percent of Postbank stock had been scheduled for last year, but was blocked by the tussle.

Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch said in a statement that a deal was struck between coalition parties on Thursday to limit Post Office control of Postbank and set the terms of their cooperation.
"The government expects the companies to support this agreement and see that it is carried out," the government said in a statement.
"On the basis of this agreement the federal government can ensure the privatisation of Deutsche Postbank AG this year," he said.
The statement was released by Boetsch and Rainer Funke, FDP state secretary in the Justice Ministry, who led the coalition talks on the Post Office agreement.
Hans Martin Bury, postal spokesman for the opposition Social Democrats, said the agreement was "a belly-flop for the post minister" that would do little to secure jobs or post office branches.
"This minority stake will not ensure a lasting alliance between the two enterprises, which the SPD sees as necessary to maintain the post office branch network," Bury said.
The Post Office and Postbank were split off from the post ministry and set up as joint stock corporations in 1995 wholly owned by the German government but set for privatisation.
Postbank does not have its own network of branch offices, but uses counter space at post offices.
The terms of continuing this relationship have been at the centre of the dispute and one of the reasons why the Post Office had sought management control of Postbank.

Boetsch and Finance Minister Theo Waigel had originally proposed that the Post Office be allowed to take 25 percent plus one share of Postbank, giving it a blocking minority, but the new deal means Post Office will not have control.
The Post Office had allied itself with Deutsche Bank AG and Swiss insurer Swiss Re. Insurance group Colonia AG also has plans to take a 15 percent stake despite Postbank opposition.
Postbank itself had proposed a consortium including BHF Bank, insurer Volksfuersorge and building society BHW.
The agreement reached late on Thursday would allow the Post Office to take a stake of up to 17.5 percent in Postbank via a capital increase planned for January 1, 1999.

The deal also states that Postbank will pay Post Office up to 37.5 million marks ($22.2 million) more each year than the 1.1 billion marks already agreedfor use of Post Office counters to distribute its banking services. A cooperation agreement will be ready for signing by the parties on March 17.
Both the Post Office and Postbank will be represented by one member on each company's supervisory board.
-- Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150
($ = 1.691 German Marks)
